source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

surveillance_terms: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil reports dengue by semana epidemiológica (SE); always map SE to calendar date range.
SINAN data distinguishes: casos suspeitos, casos prováveis, casos confirmados — do not aggregate without labeling.
Cumulative counts reset at epidemiological year start (SE01); Q1 2024 spans SE01–SE13.
Óbitos (deaths) are separately tracked as confirmed or probable; do not conflate.
Incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) are commonly reported alongside absolute counts — capture both.
State-level (UF) and municipal-level data may be reported separately; record geographic granularity explicitly.
Brazil declared a national dengue public health emergency in February 2024 — reports from this period may use emergency-specific terminology.
Hospitalization data may be reported via SIH/SUS (hospital information system) separately from SINAN case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arboviroses counts (which include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly broken out.
Do not treat Aedes mosquito surveillance or ovitrap indices as human case counts.
Brazil reports three arboviroses (dengue, Zika, Chikungunya) in combined bulletins — extract only dengue-specific rows/tables.
Distinguish between casos notificados (notified/suspected), casos prováveis, and casos confirmados — these are not interchangeable.
Óbitos em investigação (deaths under investigation) should not be counted as confirmed deaths.
Do not conflate incidence rate with absolute case count.
Emergency decree language may inflate perceived case counts — verify against tabular data.
Municipal and state totals may overlap with national totals — avoid double-counting across geographic levels.

State-level (26 states + DF) data granularity is available and should be captured where possible for subnational_location field.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

trust_considerations: Prioritize saude.gov.br and svs.saude.gov.br as primary authoritative sources over news or secondary aggregators
PAHO reports are authoritative cross-validators but may lag Brazilian MoH data by 1–2 weeks
InfoDengue data is derived from SINAN but may have reporting delays; treat as corroborating rather than primary
Brazilian news articles should only be used if they explicitly cite official MoH or state secretariat figures with specific numbers and dates
Avoid sources that aggregate without citing primary Brazilian government data

count_semantics_notes: Brazil reports dengue by semana epidemiológica (SE); always map SE to calendar date range.
SINAN data distinguishes: casos suspeitos, casos prováveis, casos confirmados — do not aggregate without labeling.
Cumulative counts reset at epidemiological year start (SE01); Q1 2024 spans SE01–SE13.
Óbitos (deaths) are separately tracked as confirmed or probable; do not conflate.
Incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) are commonly reported alongside absolute counts — capture both.
State-level (UF) and municipal-level data may be reported separately; record geographic granularity explicitly.
Brazil declared a national dengue public health emergency in February 2024 — reports from this period may use emergency-specific terminology.
Hospitalization data may be reported via SIH/SUS (hospital information system) separately from SINAN case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arboviroses counts (which include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly broken out.
Do not treat Aedes mosquito surveillance or ovitrap indices as human case counts.
Brazil reports three arboviroses (dengue, Zika, Chikungunya) in combined bulletins — extract only dengue-specific rows/tables.
Distinguish between casos notificados (notified/suspected), casos prováveis, and casos confirmados — these are not interchangeable.
Óbitos em investigação (deaths under investigation) should not be counted as confirmed deaths.
Do not conflate incidence rate with absolute case count.
Emergency decree language may inflate perceived case counts — verify against tabular data.
Municipal and state totals may overlap with national totals — avoid double-counting across geographic levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

count_semantics_notes: Brazil reports dengue by semana epidemiológica (SE); always map SE to calendar date range.
SINAN data distinguishes: casos suspeitos, casos prováveis, casos confirmados — do not aggregate without labeling.
Cumulative counts reset at epidemiological year start (SE01); Q1 2024 spans SE01–SE13.
Óbitos (deaths) are separately tracked as confirmed or probable; do not conflate.
Incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) are commonly reported alongside absolute counts — capture both.
State-level (UF) and municipal-level data may be reported separately; record geographic granularity explicitly.
Brazil declared a national dengue public health emergency in February 2024 — reports from this period may use emergency-specific terminology.
Hospitalization data may be reported via SIH/SUS (hospital information system) separately from SINAN case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arboviroses counts (which include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly broken out.
Do not treat Aedes mosquito surveillance or ovitrap indices as human case counts.
Brazil reports three arboviroses (dengue, Zika, Chikungunya) in combined bulletins — extract only dengue-specific rows/tables.
Distinguish between casos notificados (notified/suspected), casos prováveis, and casos confirmados — these are not interchangeable.
Óbitos em investigação (deaths under investigation) should not be counted as confirmed deaths.
Do not conflate incidence rate with absolute case count.
Emergency decree language may inflate perceived case counts — verify against tabular data.
Municipal and state totals may overlap with national totals — avoid double-counting across geographic levels.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

count_semantics_notes: Brazil reports dengue by semana epidemiológica (SE); always map SE to calendar date range.
SINAN data distinguishes: casos suspeitos, casos prováveis, casos confirmados — do not aggregate without labeling.
Cumulative counts reset at epidemiological year start (SE01); Q1 2024 spans SE01–SE13.
Óbitos (deaths) are separately tracked as confirmed or probable; do not conflate.
Incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) are commonly reported alongside absolute counts — capture both.
State-level (UF) and municipal-level data may be reported separately; record geographic granularity explicitly.
Brazil declared a national dengue public health emergency in February 2024 — reports from this period may use emergency-specific terminology.
Hospitalization data may be reported via SIH/SUS (hospital information system) separately from SINAN case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arboviroses counts (which include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly broken out.
Do not treat Aedes mosquito surveillance or ovitrap indices as human case counts.
Brazil reports three arboviroses (dengue, Zika, Chikungunya) in combined bulletins — extract only dengue-specific rows/tables.
Distinguish between casos notificados (notified/suspected), casos prováveis, and casos confirmados — these are not interchangeable.
Óbitos em investigação (deaths under investigation) should not be counted as confirmed deaths.
Do not conflate incidence rate with absolute case count.
Emergency decree language may inflate perceived case counts — verify against tabular data.
Municipal and state totals may overlap with national totals — avoid double-counting across geographic levels.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

trust_considerations: Prioritize saude.gov.br and svs.saude.gov.br as primary authoritative sources over news or secondary aggregators

count_semantics_notes: Brazil reports dengue by semana epidemiológica (SE); always map SE to calendar date range.
SINAN data distinguishes: casos suspeitos, casos prováveis, casos confirmados — do not aggregate without labeling.
Cumulative counts reset at epidemiological year start (SE01); Q1 2024 spans SE01–SE13.
Óbitos (deaths) are separately tracked as confirmed or probable; do not conflate.
Incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) are commonly reported alongside absolute counts — capture both.
State-level (UF) and municipal-level data may be reported separately; record geographic granularity explicitly.
Brazil declared a national dengue public health emergency in February 2024 — reports from this period may use emergency-specific terminology.
Hospitalization data may be reported via SIH/SUS (hospital information system) separately from SINAN case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arboviroses counts (which include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly broken out.
Do not treat Aedes mosquito surveillance or ovitrap indices as human case counts.
Brazil reports three arboviroses (dengue, Zika, Chikungunya) in combined bulletins — extract only dengue-specific rows/tables.
Distinguish between casos notificados (notified/suspected), casos prováveis, and casos confirmados — these are not interchangeable.
Óbitos em investigação (deaths under investigation) should not be counted as confirmed deaths.
Do not conflate incidence rate with absolute case count.
Emergency decree language may inflate perceived case counts — verify against tabular data.
Municipal and state totals may overlap with national totals — avoid double-counting across geographic levels.

Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Ministério da Saúde do Brasil (MS/SVS) epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and SINAN surveillance outputs reporting Dengue human cases, deaths, and hospitalizations in Brazil for Q1 2024 (SE 01–SE 13).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: SVS/MS is the primary national authority for dengue surveillance in Brazil. Boletins Epidemiológicos and Informes Técnicos published weekly or periodically during Jan–Mar 2024 are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, suspected, and unspecified case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations at national and subnational levels.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

collection_spec.data_focus: human Dengue case, outbreak, and surveillance data
collection_spec.user_request: Collect Dengue cases, deaths, dates, locations, source URLs, source types, and evidence quotes for Brazil from 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.

surveillance_terms: Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação
count_semantics_notes: Brazil reports dengue by semana epidemiológica (SE); always map SE to calendar date range.
SINAN data distinguishes: casos suspeitos, casos prováveis, casos confirmados — do not aggregate without labeling.
Cumulative counts reset at epidemiological year start (SE01); Q1 2024 spans SE01–SE13.
Óbitos (deaths) are separately tracked as confirmed or probable; do not conflate.
Incidence rates (per 100,000 inhabitants) are commonly reported alongside absolute counts — capture both.
State-level (UF) and municipal-level data may be reported separately; record geographic granularity explicitly.
Brazil declared a national dengue public health emergency in February 2024 — reports from this period may use emergency-specific terminology.
Hospitalization data may be reported via SIH/SUS (hospital information system) separately from SINAN case counts.
disambiguation_risks: Do not mix dengue with aggregate arboviroses counts (which include Zika and Chikungunya) unless dengue-specific counts are explicitly broken out.
Do not treat Aedes mosquito surveillance or ovitrap indices as human case counts.
Brazil reports three arboviroses (dengue, Zika, Chikungunya) in combined bulletins — extract only dengue-specific rows/tables.
Distinguish between casos notificados (notified/suspected), casos prováveis, and casos confirmados — these are not interchangeable.
Óbitos em investigação (deaths under investigation) should not be counted as confirmed deaths.
Do not conflate incidence rate with absolute case count.
Emergency decree language may inflate perceived case counts — verify against tabular data.
Municipal and state totals may overlap with national totals — avoid double-counting across geographic levels.
suggested_query_terms: dengue casos óbitos Brasil primeiro trimestre 2024
suggested_query_templates: "dengue" "primeiro trimestre" OR "1º trimestre" "2024" Brasil óbitos internações

Brazilian federal bulletins are published in Portuguese; ensure extraction pipeline handles Portuguese-language tabular data and terminology.
SINAN microdata may have reporting lag; bulletins published in Q1 2024 may undercount final Q1 totals — note data completeness status when extracting.
State-level (26 states + DF) data granularity is available and should be captured where possible for subnational_location field.
PAHO publishes regional dengue updates that include Brazil-specific data — these serve as strong validation sources against national MS/SVS figures.

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Dengue from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Dengue.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify Secretarias Estaduais de Saúde (SES) and Secretarias Municipais de Saúde (SMS) bulletins or situation reports for high-burden Brazilian states (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo) covering Jan–Mar 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational health secretariats publish state- and municipality-level dengue data that may not be fully disaggregated in national reports. These are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/OPAS Dengue situation reports, epidemiological alerts, and regional updates covering Brazil for the period 2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO publishes regular dengue situation reports for the Americas that include Brazil-specific case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and serotype data. These serve as both collection and cross-validation sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases (e.g., DATASUS/TabNet, InfoDengue, Mosqlimate, ProMED) containing dengue case and death counts for Brazil Q1 2024 to cross-validate extracted records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases provide independently aggregated counts that can be compared against extracted records from official bulletins without risk of circular validation. InfoDengue and Mosqlimate offer near-real-time epidemiological data at the municipal level.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), Global Health Observatory, or ECDC rapid risk assessments covering the Brazil dengue epidemic of early 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO and ECDC international reports provide independently compiled national-level case and death totals that can serve as held-back validation benchmarks against SVS/MS collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature, preprints, and technical reports providing case definitions, serotype distributions, severity classifications, and epidemiological context for the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected), case definitions used by SVS/MS, DENV serotype circulation (DENV-1, DENV-3 predominance in 2024), and severity thresholds (dengue com sinais de alarme, dengue grave). Essential for correct field mapping during extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED, HealthMap, or reputable news sources reporting on the Brazil dengue emergency declaration and epidemic trajectory in Q1 2024 for situational context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports provide timeline anchors, emergency declarations, and early outbreak signals that help contextualize the scale and timing of the epidemic for date_reported and reporting_period field interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national aggregate vs. subnational), or mixed disease reporting (arboviroses aggregate without dengue-specific disaggregation) for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Brazil's 2024 dengue epidemic generated high-volume reporting with varying aggregation levels. Sources that conflate dengue with Zika/Chikungunya, report only cumulative totals without period attribution, or lack subnational disaggregation require human judgment before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: Ministério da Saúde / Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS) publishes weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, Informes Técnicos de Dengue, and SINAN-based surveillance outputs. These are the authoritative primary source for national and subnational dengue case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and serotype data in Brazil. Q1 2024 was a declared epidemic period with high-frequency reporting.

State (SES) and municipal (SMS) health secretariats in high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná, Goiás, Bahia, Espírito Santo, Mato Grosso do Sul) publish independent epidemiological bulletins with finer geographic granularity than national reports. Essential for subnational_location and locality field population.

PAHO/OPAS publishes Dengue Situation Reports for the Americas with country-level and sometimes subnational breakdowns. The 2024 Brazil epidemic was a major PAHO reporting focus. These reports provide independently compiled case and death totals with explicit date attribution.

WHO Disease Outbreak News and ECDC rapid risk assessments provide independently compiled national-level dengue case and death totals for Brazil that serve as held-back validation benchmarks. These are not primary collection sources but provide cross-check capability.

DATASUS/TabNet (SINAN dengue microdata), InfoDengue (Fiocruz/PROCC), and Mosqlimate provide structured, queryable dengue surveillance datasets at municipal and state level. These enable independent validation of extracted case counts and support subnational granularity.

Peer-reviewed studies and preprints on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic provide case definitions, serotype data (DENV-1, DENV-3), severity classifications, and epidemiological context. Useful for interpreting count semantics and validating field mapping decisions.

Reputable news sources (G1/Globo, Folha de S.Paulo, Reuters, AP) and ProMED/HealthMap alerts reported on the Brazil 2024 dengue epidemic with specific case and death figures, often citing official sources. Useful for early outbreak signals and timeline anchoring when official bulletins are delayed.

iterative_search_queries.query: PAHO OPAS dengue Brazil 2024 situation report cases deaths outbreak January February March

These provide cross-validated case and death counts, often with subnational breakdowns and case classification details.
